nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $u$ has a leftmost derivation in $g$ to a word of terminals $w$, then $u$ derives $w$ in $g$ (by zero or more rewriting steps).
nodes.title: Leftmost derivations are derivations

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $u$ a word of terminals. If $u$ has a leftmost derivation in $g$ with list of rules $\rho$ to a word of terminals $w$, then $\rho$ is the empty list and $w = u$.
nodes.title: Leftmost derivations from a word of terminals are empty

nodes.summary: The example language is the union of `a ^ n b ^ n c ^ *` and `a ^ * b ^ n c ^ n`.
nodes.title: Inherently ambiguous example as a union of two languages

nodes.summary: The language `{a ^ i b ^ j c ^ k | i = j or j = k}` over the alphabet `Fin 3` (`0, 1, 2` for `a, b, c`): the standard inherently ambiguous context-free language.
nodes.title: Canonical inherently ambiguous context-free language

nodes.summary: A context-free grammar $g$ is ambiguous if some word of terminals $w$ has two leftmost derivations from the start symbol of $g$ that use different lists of rules.
nodes.title: Ambiguous grammar

nodes.summary: A language is inherently ambiguous when it is context-free and every grammar generating it is ambiguous.
nodes.title: Inherently ambiguous language

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar, $u$ a sentential form of $g$, $w$ a word of terminals and $r_1, \dots, r_n$ a list of rules over the terminals and nonterminals of $g$. The list $r_1, \dots, r_n$ is a leftmost derivation of $w$ from $u$ in $g$ when every $r_i$ is a production of $g$, and, starting from $u$ and for $i = 1, \dots, n$ in turn, the leftmost nonterminal of the current sentential form is the left-hand…
nodes.title: Leftmost derivation

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a word of terminals $w$ has a leftmost derivation in $g$ from the start symbol of $g$, then $w$ belongs to the language of $g$.
nodes.title: Words with a leftmost derivation lie in the language

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
